customer-alex: Hey, hitting intermittent 400s + huge tail latency on the embeddings endpoint since yesterday. Some requests succeed quickly, others hang ~6-8s then return 400 with 'dimension mismatch'. Customer workload is all 1536-dim. Any ideas?

support-ops: Sorry about that Alex — can you paste a failing request sample (no secrets) and the X-Request-ID from the response headers? Also did you change model or client SDK recently?

customer-alex: Here's a minimal repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["foo","bar"]}'
```
Response header: `x-request-id: r-9a7c4bf`

devon: thx. I pulled r-9a7c4bf logs. Pattern: request queued, then retried 3x by client (HTTP 429/503) -> retries land back on embeddings route -> dynamically batched with older requests -> on 2nd attempt model backend returns dim error for that bundle. Looks like a retry loop + dynamic batching mixing variants/partial payloads causing the runtime to see a mismatched batch shape.

sre-jen: confirming, saw tail latency spikes correlated with heavy retry bursts from same client token between 23:10-23:25 UTC. Dynbatch coalescing window widened under load and we folded a previous smaller-dim payload into a larger batch because the retry path re-enqueued the request without the size marker.

eng-ml-raj: short explanation: our embedding batcher validates dim per-batch but if a retry picks up a different route/variant (e.g., model fallback to open-embed-1024) the runtime will mark the batch invalid and throw a dimension mismatch once kernel shapes are set. Retries amplify this by increasing queue mix.

support-ops: ok actionable items: 1) Alex, can you confirm client SDK retry policy (max_retries, backoff) and whether you set `prefer_alt_model` or model aliasing? 2) We'll patch a defensive check in routing to drop/redirect incompatible retries instead of batching them.

customer-alex: client is using our internal SDK with default retries (5 with exponential jitter). We recently enabled a gradual alias fallback for cost so some traffic can hit a 1024 variant if 1536 not available.

devon: that's the smoking gun — alias fallback + aggressive retries. For immediate mitigation: set SDK max_retries=1 and add `x-client-model: open-embed-1536` header to pin model. Also we can temporarily set route config: `coalesce_window_ms: 5` and `max_batch_size: 64` for your org to reduce the window where mixed variants can be coalesced.

support-ops: we've applied a temporary org override: max_batch_size=64, coalesce_window_ms=5 for token REDACTED-T. Should reduce tail spikes within minutes. We'll also add a server-side guard to reject enqueued retry requests that advertise a different model alias than the active batch.

sre-jen: posted findings to infra: infra-bot triggered a canary deploy of the guard change to 3 hosts. Watch logs: `/logs?query=route:embeddings AND request_id:r-9a7c4bf` for any new dim errors after deploy.

infra-bot: deploy canary started — canary_id: c-2026-03-16-emb-guard — rolling to 3/20 hosts.

eng-ml-raj: longer-term we should tag requests with model-fingerprint at enqueue so retries can't be mixed into incompatible batches. Also we can expose a route-level `reject_mismatched_retries: true` toggle. I'll open RFC.

support-ops: Alex, once your SDK change is live can you test and post a new x-request-id if you still see a failure? We'll keep the org override until the canary is healthy.

customer-alex: switching retries to 1 and pin header now. Will run load test and update in ~10m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
